1

What you are working on

Use your deal register

Keep every deal in one workbook you own. The tool reads it where it is — nothing is uploaded, nothing is written back — and fills this step, the projections, the lending-policy check and the draft.

1
Get the template

An Excel workbook: a Start here sheet with the menu, Settings, a sheet each for term investments, call accounts and MMFs, loans and pooled funds, a Projections sheet laid out as this tool’s figures grid, a Dashboard with charts that checks what you have typed, and a Benchmark sheet that draws the liability benchmark and the Code’s five charts from the projection. Example rows show the way; replace them with your own.

2
Fill it in Excel

One row per deal, with the words from the drop-downs. Keep matured deals and repaid loans in: they are the period’s activity. The note at the top of each sheet says what every column means, a cell that is wrong or missing is marked as you type, and the Ready to read? panel on Start here says whether the tool will read the workbook as it stands and what to put right. The workbook is the record: whatever it holds — the deals, and the projection if you fill that sheet — the tool reads and locks; whatever it does not, you type here.

3
Point the tool at it

Choose the workbook. Chrome and Edge keep a link to it, so re-reading picks up what you save; elsewhere you choose it again.

See it first. — the template as it comes, example rows and all, into this report. Remove it when you have seen enough.

In the draft

The rows and maturity grids on this step are filled from the register and locked while it is in use: change the workbook and re-read it, or remove the register to type by hand. The register’s charts are on the tabs beside Debt and Investments: investments, borrowing, the year ends and the months ahead, and the period’s activity.

Nothing in the workbook leaves your computer. The report keeps a snapshot of the rows it read, so the file is not needed to open the report again.
